statement: The exact first-order horizontal zeta-ratio norm is a weighted multiplicity statistic under RH; an order-one Schur/Poisson mass identity connects the published approximation norm to local beta-integral profiles at zeros.
compatible_assumptions: RH, fixed actual xi zero set, both signs counted separately, positive real epsilon→0, complete real-line Poisson weight. No moving zero configuration, spacing or simplicity assumption.
already_proved: Scoped independent reconstruction of the exact slope and its minimum iff simplicity, with two different global-tail arguments and a negative control.
conjectural_or_unresolved: Historical priority and effective remainder; whether any independently established estimate can force the minimum for actual zeta remains entirely unresolved.
next_precise_step: Search later ratio/Hardy literature; derive an explicit oepsilon remainder under stated quantitative zero-gap/multiplicity/tail hypotheses.
potential_counterexamples: F=exp(w²) shows failure if order-one paired-product mass identity is omitted; finite epsilon agreement cannot exclude a high multiple zero.
tests: Exact beta-integral identities; rational finite paired-zero model stress tests; ordinary numerics only as checks, not proof.
significance: Reusable RH-conditional multiplicity diagnostic and resolution of a precise source question at the reconstruction level; novelty unassessed.
difficulty: Proof is self-contained given classical xi product and Poisson facts; effective rates and arithmetic simplicity remain difficult.
